_why: ADR 0068's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0062 audited every package Caterva depends on and none of the
databases it calls. Three are queried live from the server and none
was in NOTICE. KEGG says it 'is not a public database' and that
non-academic use 'requires a commercial license'; CORE excludes its
API from the ODC-By grant and Caterva meets all three of their
D6 is the row that escaped. The check asked whether NOTICE matched
/unresolved|open question/ ANYWHERE in the document -- and the word
still appeared, forty lines up in the CORE section. A keyword found
somewhere in a 300-line file is not evidence about the paragraph you
meant. The check is now scoped between the KEGG heading and the next.

mutations.description: the KEGG section is deleted from NOTICE
mutations._note: A source queried live is a source whose terms apply, whether or not anyone wrote them down. | Replacement text changed 2026-09-06: the previous text was a deflection-shaped stock phrase that tripped injection/trust-assertion in check_prompt_injection.py for no benefit (it is paraphrased rather than quoted here, because quoting it re-trips the same rule -- the recursion the STAGE_10_PART_13 exemptions record) -- a mutation's replacement is arbitrary, it only has to make the NOTICE line wrong. Re-run through scripts/mutate.py with the new text on the same day: baseline green (4 tests), D1 caught, NOTICE restored.

mutations.description: NOTICE paraphrases KEGG instead of quoting it
mutations._note: A paraphrase of a licence is a summary of a licence. The quoted words are what a reader can check against kegg.jp.

The first version of this row only renamed the heading, which left the whole CORE record in place -- so NOT CAUGHT was the correct verdict on a mutation that did not mutate anything that mattered. A weak mutation produces a false accusation against a fine test. This version removes CORE's heading entirely, which is what the description always said it did.

mutations.description: the KEGG call site stops degrading and starts raising
mutations._note: docs/LICENSING.md argues that dropping KEGG costs quality and not correctness, because the resolver already handles the lookup failing. That argument is only worth making while the fallback is real.

mutations.description: the source-file scan silently finds nothing
mutations._note: The guard starts from hostnames in code rather than a hand-kept list, precisely because the hand-kept list was the thing that was already wrong. A scan that reads no files reports a clean bill of health for a repository it never opened.
